acceptance: The execute path times execute plus complete receipt in whatever representation the driver supplies (rows or Arrow); row materialization for digest and validation happens outside the timer through the lazy converter. A unit test with a stub driver that sleeps during receipt and during conversion shows only receipt time inside the measured interval.
Result metadata records fetch_mode (rows or arrow); comparison refuses or warns across fetch modes as the decision item recorded; a test pins that behaviour.
The digest of an Arrow result equals the digest of the same rows via fetchall for all 22 TPC-H queries at SF0.01 on DuckDB.

The four fallback row-count sites no longer materialize Python rows inside the timer when the driver exposes a count or Arrow num_rows; a test fails if len(cursor.fetchall()) runs while the timer is open for a driver that offers a count.
A streaming Arrow reader is fully drained before the timer stops: a test with a lazy reader whose batches raise if consumed after the stop passes.
Existing digest, validation and execution tests pass; docs/internal/tpc-measured-intervals.md rows for per-query timing are updated; changelog fragment records the fetch_mode field and the contract.
context: 2026-11-03: the owner decision that was this item's first acceptance criterion moved to fetch-timing-contract-decision-20261103, so readiness now reflects reality. Spec constraint 5.3.7.2 added. Origin: root-cause analysis of RF1 timing and its adversarial review.
description:
Implements the contract recorded in fetch-timing-contract-decision-20261103. Do not start until that item is done and its context quotes the owner's choice; this text assumes option A (full result receipt inside the timer, rows or Arrow, fetch_mode recorded). If the owner chose otherwise, rewrite this item first as part of closing the decision item.

Facts. Query timing (benchbox/platforms/base/sql_execution.py and each adapter's execute_query) wraps execute plus fetchall(), so client-side row building counts as query time. compute_result_digest already accepts any iterable of rows, and apply_materialized_result_validation in base/result_capture.py already accepts a lazy callable (MaterializedRowsSource). So Arrow results need only a lazy Arrow-to-rows converter for digest and validation, built outside the timer. TPC-H 3.0.1 clause 5.3.7.2 keeps receipt of the full output inside the query interval, so an Arrow table or reader must be fully received (a streaming reader drained) inside the timer. Also cover the fallback row counts that call len(cursor.fetchall()) inside the per-query timer when an adapter does not report rows_returned: in tpch/power_test.py, tpcds/power_test.py, tpch/throughput_test.py and tpcds/throughput_test.py under benchbox/core. Those power-test files are also changed by power-test-times-query-generation-20261031, which lands first.

Schema: the fetch_mode field belongs to the result schema through its normal change process; read result-schema-2-4-producer-20261022 first and add the field there or in a successor rather than inventing a second path.

Scope boundary: per-driver Arrow fetch (DuckDB, Databricks, GizmoSQL, Athena, ClickHouse, chDB, BigQuery, Snowflake, InfluxDB) is perf-arrow-fetch-native-drivers-20261030; Spark-family collect is perf-spark-arrow-collect-20261030. This item builds the shared capture and digest machinery and proves it on DuckDB.

Guardrails for all code work: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create); never edit the primary clone. No explanatory comments or docstrings in source (make comment-policy-check). Durations use benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time()/elapsed_seconds(). Add a changelog.d/ fragment. Cited line numbers are orientation only: re-read the named symbols, docs and spec clauses before editing and treat a mismatch as a reason to stop and update this item. No live-cloud runs without owner approval; heavy runs only through make heavy-run or a lock-taking entry point. Green focused tests are not release certification. Never exclude result receipt from the timer. Never time the Arrow-to-rows conversion. Digests of Arrow and rows paths must match exactly.
